claims.text: Introducing controlled porosity into as-cast HfMoTaTiZr can reduce its density.
Controlled porosity can reduce density without sacrificing the mechanical properties of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed intervention is the introduction of controlled porosity.
The intervention is intended to operate from room temperature through elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
Porosity is the structural mediator produced by the intervention.
Introducing porosity reduces the overall density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The material's strength can be maintained because its microstructure is preserved after porosity is introduced.
The distribution of porosity can help maintain the material's strength.
The porous material is predicted to have lower density than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The porous material is predicted to show no significant loss of mechanical properties at room temperature.
The porous material is predicted to show no significant loss of mechanical properties at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The proposed loading boundary is limited to conditions that do not compromise the material's structure.
The optimal amount and distribution of porosity are uncertain.
The effect of porosity on long-term material stability is uncertain.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing density and mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr specimens with and without controlled porosity under the specified temperatures.
